title: The Friendly Monster Under the Bed
summary: When Mateo hears a tiny noise under his bed, he discovers that the monster living there is hiding a secret a lot like his own.

scenes.text: Mateo snuggled down under the blankets. Through the window came the light of the moon, round and silver. Outside, the wind rocked the trees very gently. Everything was calm... until, from under the bed, came a tiny little noise. A shiver. A sigh. Mateo lay very still, listening to his own heartbeat. What could that shy little sound be, there in the dark?

Very carefully, Mateo peeked over the edge of the bed. And there, between an old ball and a slipper, were two big, shiny eyes. It was a monster. But it did not roar or look scary: it was curled up, hugging its knees, trembling. When it saw Mateo, it let out a frightened whisper: Please, don't hurt me. Mateo blinked, surprised. The monster seemed even more scared than he was.

I won't hurt you, said Mateo softly. Why are you shivering? The monster looked down. It's just... I'm very afraid of the dark, it confessed. Down here everything is black, and when the light goes out, I feel so alone. Mateo's eyes went wide. He felt exactly the same way! That was why he always left the door open a little. The two of them laughed softly, surprised to be so alike.

Mateo had an idea. From under his pillow he pulled out his little star flashlight and switched it on. Plink! A whole scatter of light stars appeared on the ceiling, soft and golden. Look, he said, now the dark isn't so scary. The monster gazed up, amazed, and its trembling slowly faded away. I've never seen anything so beautiful, it murmured. And then Mateo lent it his softest teddy bear, so it wouldn't feel alone.

That night, the monster did not stay under the bed. It curled up beside Mateo, with the teddy bear between them. The moon watched over them from the window, and the little stars still glowed on the ceiling. Goodnight, friend, yawned Mateo. Goodnight, answered the monster, almost asleep already. The two of them breathed slowly, very close together, and little by little they closed their eyes. No one was afraid anymore: there was only the quiet night, warm and soft, watching over them until morning.
